# Froe

> A Rust CLI and library for reading and maintaining Apache Jackrabbit Oak segment stores (segment-tar / TarMK), including those used by AEM. Directly from disk: no running Oak instance, no JVM.

Read commands take no lock and write nothing, so they work on a live or stopped repository. Maintenance (compaction, backup, restore, journal recovery, checkpoints) needs a stopped repository and an exclusive lock, and asks for confirmation. Exports produce JSON lines, Parquet or SQLite, so repository content can be queried with full SQL in DuckDB or SQLite: COUNT, GROUP BY, HAVING, CTEs, window functions and joins, with no dependence on Oak indexes and no load on the running instance. Oak's own JCR-SQL2 has none of those aggregates or CTEs, and traverses the repository when no index covers a query.

## Docs

- [The site, in markdown](https://froe.sh/index.md): The same account as the homepage, without the page chrome.
- [Source](https://github.com/koraytaylan/froe): The CLI, the core library and the documentation. Apache-2.0 license.
- [Releases](https://github.com/koraytaylan/froe/releases/latest): Prebuilt binaries, SHA256SUMS and the changelog.
- [API reference](https://docs.rs/froe): The core crate's repository traversal API.

## Optional

- [Working with a store](https://froe.sh/index.md#commands): Inspect, export, maintain and index commands.
- [Download](https://froe.sh/index.md#download): Prebuilt Linux, macOS and Windows binaries from the latest GitHub release.
- [Build from source](https://froe.sh/index.md#build): Clone, `cargo build --release`, one binary.
- [SQL over an AEM repository export](https://froe.sh/index.md#examples): Twenty-five DuckDB and SQLite recipes for auditing exported content: component, template, tag and asset usage across pages, stale and redirecting pages, DAM formats, content fragment models and more.
- [Implementation & reference](https://froe.sh/index.md#reference): Store versions, Oak interoperability and the storage-format, maintenance, index and feature-map documents.
